author: hndrk
text:
He Salivan,

Do you think it would be a good idea to factor in average spread on buys?

I mean the bid might reach your level, but the ask might not.

And also, do you find that price often misses your level by a pip or so?

If the average deviation from the levels is about one pip it might be an idea

to have one position exactly on the level and one position; the level plus one.

I know you are trying to get perfect entries and exits on your trades, but it really sucks

to miss a perfect entry/exit on a massive trade by just one pip.

Of course if you find this rarely happens then it's not an issue.

author: hndrk
text:
Hello Salivan,

With 'average spread' I mean that if the spread on a pair stays around 1
 pip most of the time than I would call the average spread on that pair 1
 pip.

And with spread I mean the difference between the buy price and the sell price.

So if the average spread on a pair is one pip than for a buy limit I would add that to my entry point to ensure a fill.

Example: If my level is 1.00 and the average spread is 0.10 then my buy limit is at 1.10.

Thank you.
